test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 13 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which Act transferred the power of governance from the East India Company to the British Crown?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Government of India Act, 1858**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Government of India Act, 1858** marked the end of the East India Company’s rule and transferred the administration of India directly to the British Crown.
 
• The act established the position of a **Secretary of State for India**, who was responsible for overseeing Indian affairs in Britain.
 
• It introduced the **Council of India** to assist the Secretary of State, comprising 15 members, mainly former directors of the East India Company.
 
• This act formally ended the dual governance system and centralized power under the British government, following the failure of the East India Company during the **1857 Revolt**.
 
• The Governor-General of India was renamed as **Viceroy of India**, representing the Crown directly in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Charter Act, 1833**

 
 
• This act centralized legislative powers in India by establishing a single legislative council for all British territories in India.
 
• It marked the end of the East India Company's trading rights and made it an administrative body.
 
• It introduced the idea of an open competition for civil services, but the provision was not implemented until later.
 
 
 
• **Regulating Act, 1773**
 
 
• This was the first attempt by the British government to regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India.
 
• It established a Governor-General in Bengal and created a Supreme Court at Fort William, Kolkata.
 
• The act aimed to curb corruption and mismanagement but had limited success.
 
 
 
• **Pitt's India Act, 1784**
 
 
• This act introduced the concept of dual control between the British government and the East India Company.
 
• It created a Board of Control to supervise civil, military, and revenue administration in India.
 
• The act aimed to address issues of governance after the shortcomings of the Regulating Act.
 
 
 
• **Indian Rebellion of 1857**
 
 
• The widespread uprising against British rule revealed the flaws in the East India Company's administrative structure.
 
• It directly led to the implementation of the Government of India Act, 1858, which centralized power under the Crown.
 
• The rebellion is considered one of the most significant events in Indian history, leading to the dissolution of the East India Company.
